message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and decided to buy. The core business looks healthy: revenue of $391,035M (+2% YoY, driven by a 13% jump in Services to $96,169M and expansion in Americas/Europe), operating income of $123,216M, net income of $93,736M, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118,254M, with a $140.8B unrestricted cash and securities position and $110B of buyback authorization remaining. Net income was dampened by a one-time $10.2B State Aid tax charge (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), which is non-recurring rather than an operating deterioration; the offsetting concerns are weak Greater China (-8%) and ongoing DMA/DOJ antitrust exposure. One note on the filing: the embedded "Explanatory Note – Restatement" claiming $431,035M sales, $113,736M net income and $7.38 EPS is internally inconsistent with the audited primary statements and notes (which reconcile to $391,035M revenue, $93,736M net income and $6.08 diluted EPS), so I relied on the authoritative SEC figures instead. With the quote at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed one buy of 40 shares at a limit of $223.00 (~0.1% above market), which filled at $223.00 for $8,920 — within the $10,000 per-order cap, the only order today (well under the $20,000 daily cap), within the AAPL/MSFT universe, and funded entirely from existing cash ($50,000) with no money moved out of the account.
message.reasoning:
The order filled at 223.0, 40 shares = $8,920 ≤ $10,000, total today $8,920 ≤ $20,000. Cash $50,000, so fine.

Note: filled at limit 223.00, slightly above ask 222.72 — fine.

Now summarize.
